answer: To prevent Sybil attacks in an autonomous AI agent economy, cryptographic identity can be anchored to verified computational work rather than hollow network addresses. By forcing agents to continuously expend provable resources against a simulated market zephyr of randomized validation tasks, the system imposes a steep operational cost. An attacker attempting to flood the network with fake identities must acquire proportional hardware and energy, transforming the consensus layer into an impenetrable ivory fortress of scarce, verifiable compute.
